claims.text: A machine-learning-guided thermomechanical processing approach can concurrently improve phase stability, microstructure refinement, and material properties.
Conventional casting or melting generally produces mixed phase distributions and relatively coarse microstructures.
Machine-learning models trained on high-throughput experimental and simulation data can predict thermomechanical processing parameters such as temperature profiles, strain rates, and energy inputs.
Robust datasets are needed to calibrate models for controlled thermomechanical treatment.
Refined grain boundaries and controlled phase interfaces direct microstructural evolution.
The proposed processing stabilizes refined grain boundaries and controlled phase interfaces.
Machine learning can identify processing windows that optimally balance kinetic and thermodynamic factors.
The identified processing windows minimize deleterious phase decomposition.
The identified processing windows promote dynamic recrystallization.
The identified processing windows promote grain refinement.
An optimized microstructure can enhance mechanical and functional properties.
Compared with conventional thermomechanical routes, ML-optimized processing will improve phase stability.
Compared with conventional thermomechanical routes, ML-optimized processing will produce a finer and more uniform microstructure.
Compared with conventional thermomechanical routes, ML-optimized processing will increase both strength and ductility.
Traditional thermomechanical processing typically targets only one or two of phase stability, microstructure refinement, and property optimization.
Conventional processing often improves strength at the expense of ductility.
The approach is likely effective only where sufficient experimental and simulation data exist for robust model training.
The approach may be unreliable for extremely complex phase behavior or processing conditions far outside the model's training domain.
High-throughput data and preliminary simulation studies support the proposed ML-guided thermomechanical concept.
The magnitude of improvement and universal applicability across diverse alloy systems remain unestablished.
